title: convert_v1_to_v2_response drops existing v2 operands and silently omits unlisted object types

blocks.heading: convert_v1_to_v2_response drops existing v2 operands and silently omits unlisted object types

blocks.text: The `convert_v1_to_v2_response` helper translates ZPA policy rule conditions into v2 request shape. When given operands that are already in v2 format (`values` or `entry_values`), it extracts nothing and returns `[]`. Operands whose object type is not in `_V1_TO_V2_VALUE_TYPES` or `_V1_TO_V2_ENTRY_TYPES` are also silently dropped, with no error or warning.

blocks.heading: Bug 1: already-v2 condition input returns an empty list
Bug 2: unlisted object type is silently dropped

blocks.item: Expected: operands carrying `values` or `entry_values` are preserved.
Expected: the `UNKNOWN_TYPE` operand is preserved, or an explicit error is raised.

blocks.text: `convert_v1_to_v2_response` is called by `get_rule` in `src/zscaler_mcp/tools/zpa/_policy_common.py` (line 135) and by `normalize_v2_rule_response` in `zpa_helpers.py` (line 279).

In read-convert-update flows, where a caller reads a rule via `zpa_get_access_policy_rule` and passes the returned `conditions` into `zpa_update_access_policy_rule`, existing v2 operands or unlisted criteria are stripped before the write is submitted.

blocks.item: Lines 233–241 only inspect `operand.get("rhs")` and `operand.get("lhs")`. If operands already use `values` or `entry_values`, `rhs` is `None`, so nothing is collected. Lines 251–252 then skip appending because `new_operands` is empty.
Lines 233 and 237 only check the hardcoded sets `_V1_TO_V2_VALUE_TYPES` and `_V1_TO_V2_ENTRY_TYPES` (lines 185–209). Any operand with an unlisted `object_type` is skipped.
Pass through operands that already contain `values` or `entry_values`.
For unknown object types, pass them through or raise an error instead of silently dropping them.
Add unit tests covering v1 input, v2 input, mixed input, and unknown object types.

blocks.text: Related to #109 (`convert_v2_to_sdk_format` returning `[]` for flat condition dicts).
